key_insight: With 10 labeled examples per class, multimodal large language models outperformed vision foundation and vision-language models trained on the same examples in most ophthalmic imaging tasks.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest a potential route to developing ophthalmic image-analysis tools when labeled data are scarce, but do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Retrospective benchmark across 4 public and 3 private ophthalmic imaging datasets.
Compared 9 models across multimodal language, vision foundation, and vision-language architectures.
Evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot language models against vision models adapted with 10-shot or full-data training.
evidence_signal: For retinal OCT classification, 10-shot multimodal language models achieved macro-F1 0.94, versus 0.59 for 10-shot vision models and 0.96 for full-data vision models.
watch_item: Retrospective benchmark performance does not establish prospective clinical safety or reliability across real-world imaging settings.
paper_title: Ophthalmic AI With Just Ten Examples: Comparing Multimodal Large Language Models, Vision Foundation Models, and Vision-Language Models
